findings.finding: Three change items write the same file under mutually exclusive instructions. CHG-c75db8cc, CHG-fcaecb5a and CHG-b70214ce all target src/features/example/Screen.js, and each intent begins 'Realize only this source requirement:' followed by a different requirement — the toggle behaviour, the 402x874 geometry, and the 'Zones corporelles' title respectively. Read literally, each instruction forbids realizing the other two in the same file, yet the file must simultaneously carry the Existing re-export, render() and toggle(), and boundaries.write_scope lists src/features/example/Screen.js exactly once with change_kind MODIFY. No plan item, constraint or rationale states that the three intents compose into a single delivery of that file, so the only instruction an implementer can follow without violating one of the three is left to inference.
evidence: consumers/4.js buildPlanContract derives one change item per changed impact per requirement and validates each intent only with V.assertUnicodeExactText; nothing mechanically reconciles several single-requirement intents that resolve to the same path.

findings.finding: The geometry contract is satisfiable at markup level while being unsatisfiable at measurement level, because the box model of the frame is never pinned. The FUNCTIONAL_TEST asserts the declared CSS 'width:402px' and 'height:874px' in the returned HTML string, whereas the VISUAL_COMPARE asserts an unadjusted getBoundingClientRect equal to 402 and 874 with tolerance 0. getBoundingClientRect returns border-box dimensions, but the CSS default is box-sizing: content-box. If the implementer adds any border or padding to element 4478:7209 while styling the contained title, the declared values still read exactly 402px/874px and the Node assertions pass, while the measured rect becomes larger than 402x874 and both viewports fail at tolerance 0. The implementation_constraints fix the declared values, the two viewports and observer independence, but never constrain box-sizing, border or padding on the frame, so the delivery has no stated way to make the two obligations agree by construction.

planContract implementation_constraints last entry ends: 'Geometry is fixed 402px by 874px at both 402x874 and 503x971 viewports.' — no box-sizing, border or padding constraint anywhere in the three plan items.

findings.required_correction: Add an implementation constraint to PLAN-a5257953e0c6d497bcfa1ca3, mirrored in PLAN-fb62ec2c94827d251048da3d and PLAN-fb6e814aa7f62034e4f94ca4 since all three write the same file, pinning the box model of element 4478:7209 so the declared value and the measured border-box rect are provably the same number at tolerance 0: require box-sizing: border-box on the frame with zero border and zero padding, or content-box with border and padding explicitly zero, and state that the frame must not inherit a box model from the orchestration-supplied host page.

findings.finding: The plan mandates a containment relation in its implementation intent that no criterion, assertion or proof can falsify. Every Screen.js change item requires markup for a frame data-figma-id="4478:7209" 'containing title data-figma-id="4953:6611"', and the frozen Figma tree does make 4953:6611 a descendant of 4478:7209 (4478:7209 -> 4953:6606 -> 4953:6608 -> 4953:6611). But CRT-bc8b21bd carries only the CONTENT assertion AST-a8094db4 on the characters, CRT-1f4fb9b8 carries only the two GEOMETRY assertions on the frame, and neither the FUNCTIONAL_TEST nor the VISUAL_COMPARE expected text requires the title node to be inside the frame node. A delivery rendering the title as a sibling of the frame satisfies every stated obligation, including both viewports at tolerance 0. Either the containment is part of the mandated delivery, in which case it must be provable, or it is outside the declared three-property disposable scope, in which case the intent should not mandate it.
evidence: Frozen Figma node table: node 4953:6611 parent 4953:6608, whose parent is 4953:6606, whose parent is 4478:7209 — containment is a genuine property of the observed source.

findings.finding: The evidentiary chain from the delivered code to the measured pixels is never closed. Both VISUAL_COMPARE proofs measure a DOM rendered from an orchestration-generated rendered.html, but no obligation binds that host page to the output of the delivered Screen.render(). PROOF-3523c76e requires measuring the unadjusted getBoundingClientRect of 4478:7209 at 402x874 and 503x971 and retaining rendered.png and browser-facts.json, yet the retained evidence is not required to record the provenance of the markup that was measured. The only link is free-text in implementation_constraints ('Orchestration supplies the independent browser observer ... its generated rendered.html host page'), which is an assertion of fact, not a verifiable obligation on the delivery. The FUNCTIONAL_TEST counterparts explicitly disclaim the other half ('This Node check observes markup, not rendered geometry'). A delivery could therefore pass both VISUAL_COMPARE proofs while the measured document was not produced from the delivered render(), and the plan's own falsification design (tolerance 0 plus a second independent viewport) would not detect it.
evidence: consumers/4.js normalizeProofObligations validates only that proof.expected is non-empty exact text (V.assertUnicodeExactText) and that non-FUNCTIONAL_TEST proofs have target_test_impact_id === null; no mechanical check constrains the semantic content of a VISUAL_COMPARE expectation.

Retain rendered.png and browser-facts.json at each viewport.' — no provenance of the measured document is required in the retained artefacts.

planContract implementation_constraints (identical in all three plan items): 'Orchestration supplies the independent browser observer scripts/kodjo/lib/vnext-figma-browser-observer.js, its generated rendered.html host page ... The implementation exports render() from src/features/example/Screen.js with zero arguments returning an HTML string' — the derivation of rendered.html from render() is stated, never proven.
findings.required_correction: Extend the expected of PROOF-3523c76e7bc3fda9b4a844e9 and of PROOF-2562651b860363b4d1ba6e2b to require browser-facts.json, at each of the two viewports, to record the provenance of the measured document: the SHA-256 of the exact Screen.render() string captured at observation time and the SHA-256 of the document actually loaded by the observer, together with the requirement that the two correspond. Observer independence must be preserved: the implementation must still neither write nor adjust these artefacts, so the provenance record is produced by the orchestration driver, not by the delivery.

findings.finding: The single test file must both assert module-level toggle state and destroy that state, and the plan does not state how the two interact. TEST-cedc0702 requires, in tests/ui.test.js, (a) the toggle transitions off->on and on->off of Screen.toggle() with selection 'initially off', and (b) clearing require.cache for src/features/example/Screen.js and src/shared/ui/Existing.js, replacing the shared module's cached Existing export with a sentinel, re-requiring Screen, and restoring both cache entries in finally. Re-requiring Screen yields a new module instance with its own fresh toggle state, while any Screen reference captured before the sentinel block continues to point at the previous instance. The obligation never says which instance the toggle assertions observe, nor that they must run against a freshly loaded module, so the 'initially off' precondition depends on undocumented ordering between the two blocks in one file. The same cache-mutation text is repeated verbatim in TEST-ad4e2d40 and TEST-209d3f8b alongside the render() markup assertions, so the hazard is present three times in the same file.
evidence: Observed Git object src/features/example/Screen.js at 96d967dc: 'const {Existing}=require("../../shared/ui/Existing');module.exports={Existing};' — a load-time value re-export, confirming that module identity and load order govern the observable Existing value and, once toggle state is added, the observable initial state.

planContract TEST-ad4e2d403a4197c9a62d6fc2 and TEST-209d3f8b0e7a5036e35352a0 expected: both repeat the identical require.cache sentinel paragraph, so all three obligations mutate the module registry of the same file under test.

planContract TEST-cedc0702975b374db46be747 expected: 'Selection toggles off to on and on to off ... initially off ... Verify the normal Existing value, then clear require.cache for src/shared/ui/Existing.js and src/features/example/Screen.js, require the shared module, replace its cached Existing export with a fresh unique object sentinel S, re-require Screen and assert Screen.Existing === S by reference identity. Restore both cache entries in finally.'

findings.required_correction: Make the isolation explicit in the expected of TEST-cedc0702975b374db46be747: require the toggle assertions to run against a module instance obtained after a documented cache reset, with the first call of toggle() on that instance returning true and the second returning false, and state the required ordering and mutual independence of the toggle block and the require.cache sentinel block so that neither can leave registry or module state that changes the other's outcome. Mirror the ordering statement in TEST-ad4e2d403a4197c9a62d6fc2 and TEST-209d3f8b0e7a5036e35352a0, which carry the same cache mutation.
